Rarity.rationale: Matches ReptileTrinket.cs:16. In the transcribed shared grab bag as Uncommon (relic_pools.py:126), executed by `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b13.py pool`.

CanonicalVars.rationale: ReptileTrinket.cs:18 pins `new PowerVar<StrengthPower>(3m)` and line 27 passes `DynamicVars.Strength.BaseValue`. No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 3 is the non-ascension value. BaseValue at the only call site, so there is no IntValue/BaseValue split.

AfterPotionUsed.rationale: ReptileTrinket.cs:22-29 applies `ReptileTrinketPower` with amount 3, target and applier both the owner's creature, cardSource null; reptile_trinket.py:26-29 does the same with `applier=self.player`. The power is ported and matches the source's inheritance: ReptileTrinketPower.cs:5 is `: TemporaryStrengthPower` with only an OriginModel override (presentation), and powers.py's ReptileTrinketPower is likewise a bare TemporaryStrengthPower subclass with power_type BUFF. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b13.py reptile-trinket`): one use gives [('reptile_trinket', 3), ('strength', 3)], a second stacks to 6/6, and the turn end reverts both to nothing -- which is what TemporaryStrengthPower means. SCOPE NOTE: the shared contract defers potions, but the relic's own behaviour is a Strength grant, so it is audited rather than skipped; the potion is only the trigger, the same disposition batch 1 recorded for relic/belt_buckle's potion hooks.

ExtraHoverTips.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / the N*Vfx nodes are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

guards.what: N1: `potion.Owner == base.Owner && CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress` (ReptileTrinket.cs:24) -- both dropped by the port
guards.rationale: Both are structurally satisfied rather than missing. The owner check is single-player. The IsInProgress check is the load-bearing one, and it is EXECUTED-checked rather than assumed: `grep -rn on_potion_used sts2_rl/` shows exactly one dispatch site outside hooks.py and the listeners -- combat.py:610, inside CombatState.use_potion -- so an out-of-combat potion use cannot reach this relic in the sim. Checked deliberately because the relic would otherwise apply a combat power with no combat state and crash on self.player. NOTE per binding rule 7: combat.py and hooks.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: the relic grants ReptileTrinketPower, a temporary-Strength WRAPPER, not StrengthPower directly -- and that is what makes it safe against two other relics
guards.rationale: Recorded because the wrapper is where PROMPT.md bug class 5 (temporary-power double-dip) lives. The sim's TemporaryStrengthPower applies its internal StrengthPower with NO applier argument, which is the mechanism audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json guard N2 verdicts deliberate-divergence: relic/unsettling_lamp's doubling requires `applier is self.player` and therefore skips the internal power for free, reproducing C#'s explicit HasDoubledTemporaryPowerSource guard by a different route. relic/ruined_helmet in this same batch is the other exposure and it does NOT have an applier clause -- so it doubles the internal StrengthPower on both sides, once. Executed evidence for the internal application landing at all is the [('reptile_trinket', 3), ('strength', 3)] pair above. One verdict per mechanism (binding rule 3): the double-dip equivalence is power_cmd N2's, cited here rather than re-derived. NOTE per binding rule 7: powers.py and power_cmd.json are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N3: nothing in either implementation limits the relic to once per turn or once per combat
guards.rationale: ReptileTrinket.cs has no state field and no reset hook of any kind, so `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` correctly files reptile_trinket in the 'relics holding no state at all' bucket and PROMPT.md bug class 13 has nothing to bite. The port likewise holds no state. Executed: two potion uses in one turn stack to 6, on both sides. Recorded so the absence reads as a source property rather than a dropped guard.
The 'this cannot prompt the player' context -- multiplayer plumbing, noted in the mapping rather than verdicted as a divergence, per the shared contract's scope section.
